text:
Elliot Price: quick sync in-thread on the benchmark report landing page + where methodology appendix lives. Need decisions today so we can unblock PR copy + nav.

Wei Chen: +1. main q for me: do we put the methodology appendix under /docs (so it’s clearly “how it works”), or keep everything under marketing site with an “Appendix” anchor? either is fine but we should be consistent with other benchmark content.

Ethan Wallace: from narrative POV: landing page should stay lightweight (hero, key charts, CTA, brief methodology summary) and then link out to a full methodology appendix for credibility. If appendix is too buried people won’t click.

Soojin Lee: preference: landing page on marketing domain, appendix in docs domain. We want the landing page to convert, but the appendix should read like “engineer-facing details” + be easy to cite in sales cycles.

Tessa Morgan: design-wise that split is fine. we can make a “Methodology & reproducibility” section on landing w/ a button. Just need a stable URL for the appendix so we don’t break outbound links.

Alicia Perez: +1 stable URL. also if appendix is long, we should do right-side TOC / anchor nav. helps for reviewer comments and in-page sharing.

Jonas Weber: methodology needs to be explicit: workloads, concurrency, warmup/caching policy, how latency/$ computed, variance language. I’d rather that live in docs so we can version it and point to it from future refreshes.

Claire Dubois: agree. Also we should avoid a situation where marketing edits the methodology summary and it diverges from what we ran. If appendix is docs-owned, we can treat it as source-of-truth.

Elliot Price: ok proposed structure:
1) Landing page (marketing/docs hybrid page) at `/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar` (or similar). Contains:
- hero + download PDF CTA
- “What is latency per dollar?” explainer
- headline findings (w/ soft language + variance caveat)
- chart gallery (3–5 charts) w/ links to tables
- “Methodology (summary)” section (2–3 paragraphs + bullets)
- button linking to full appendix
- FAQ (security + reproducibility)
2) Methodology appendix in docs at `/docs/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/methodology`.
3) Public table page at `/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/data` (or section on landing) – TBD based on how eng wants to host the JSON/CSV.

Wei Chen: works. minor suggestion: make appendix URL shorter, like `/docs/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar-methodology` (less nesting). but I can live with either.

Elliot Price: nesting is fine if we keep it stable + add redirects. I’ll set up redirect if we later flatten.

Soojin Lee: for landing page: we should keep PDF download above the fold + a secondary CTA “Run a consult / talk to an engineer”. But careful not to look too sales-y.

Ethan Wallace: +1. also: “View tables” CTA is important for credibility. People want the numbers, not just charts.

Alicia Perez: can we do “Download report” and “View data tables” as two buttons in hero? + a small link “Read methodology”.

Tessa Morgan: yep. also we need disclaimers near the charts: not every workload, not every region, results depend on input lengths/concurrency. keep it readable, not legalese.

Jonas Weber: pls ensure the summary doesn’t say “fastest” or “best” in absolute terms. should say “measured under X workload; see methodology”.

Wei Chen: appendix placement: I’ll draft it in docs w/ clear sections:
- Overview (what we measured)
- Workloads (chat + embeddings; prompt distributions)
- Regions + hardware notes (as much as we can say publicly)
- Runtime config (batching/caching) at a high level
- Measurement windows + warmup
- Metrics definitions (p50/p95 latency; throughput; cost per 1M tokens; derived latency/$)
- Variance + rerun policy (high level)
- How to reproduce (lightweight) + link to example repo
- Limitations

Elliot Price: perfect. also: let’s cross-link from existing docs so people can find the report without going through marketing.
Candidates:
- API docs “Performance & limits” page
- “Regions” page (where we list region header selection)
- “Observability / usage” pages (token cost breakdown)

Wei Chen: + region header docs need to be clean because appendix will reference it. I’ll add a short callout box: “Selecting a region for benchmarks / reproduction” with the exact header name + example curl.

Claire Dubois: please don’t include internal header names that differ by gateway. use what customers actually set. If there’s ambiguity, better to show both (SDK + REST) or link to region selection docs.

Elliot Price: yep. we’ll avoid anything that only exists in internal tooling.

Soojin Lee: SEO: landing page should target “LLM latency per dollar” and “inference cost vs latency” keywords. But let’s not keyword-stuff. Make sure meta title/description reflect “production economics benchmark”.

Alicia Perez: question: do we want methodology appendix to be indexed or noindex? if it’s indexed, it may rank for “latency per dollar” and compete w landing page.

Elliot Price: good call. I lean: index landing page, index appendix but canonical to landing page? Alternatively noindex appendix. Need a quick decision.

Wei Chen: I’d rather not noindex methodology. People search for “benchmark methodology” and we want them to find it. Maybe set canonical to itself, but add strong link back to landing + “Download report”.

Soojin Lee: agree w Wei. Keep it indexable. We can make landing page the primary via internal linking and nav placement.

Elliot Price: done.

Ethan Wallace: re: cross-links from existing docs: we should add a small “New: Latency/$ benchmark report” callout in the docs sidebar “Benchmarks” section. Not too loud, but discoverable.

Elliot Price: ok.

Jonas Weber: last thing: appendix should explicitly mention that we don’t publish raw request logs / customer traces. Only aggregated benchmark runs. That’s a likely question.

Wei Chen: will add under “Data handling” subsection + link to security FAQ.

Tessa Morgan: timing: design needs final section list for landing to create consistent component spacing. Elliot can you confirm the sections order?

Elliot Price: proposed landing page order:
1) Hero (headline + two CTAs: Download PDF / View tables)
2) Credibility strip (regions covered, models covered, reproducible harness link)
3) “Why latency/$” explainer (short)
4) Key findings (3 bullets + small chart)
5) Chart gallery (tabs by workload or by model family)
6) Methodology summary (bullets) + link to full appendix
7) FAQ (variance, regions, caching, security/data handling)
8) Final CTA (Hosted API quickstart + “talk to us”)

Alicia Perez: looks good. for chart gallery: tabs by workload is easier for comprehension. and make sure units are consistent across charts.

Claire Dubois: + please add a footnote that all charts report p50/p95 latency + the exact concurrency. Otherwise people will assume single-request latency.

Elliot Price: added.

Wei Chen: Action items:
- I’ll draft methodology appendix + region header snippet today EOD.
- Elliot to add cross-links from Regions + Performance pages + create /benchmarks nav item.
- Soojin/Ethan to review landing page copy for “claims language” + consistency with appendix.
- Tessa/Alicia finalize landing components once copy is in PR.

Elliot Price: :thumbsup: I’ll open the docs PR and tag everyone. let’s keep links stable: landing `/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar` and appendix `/docs/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/methodology`.

Soojin Lee: :thumbsup: pls include UTM-safe links from docs -> landing page (no UTMs in docs). UTMs only in campaign channels.

Elliot Price: yep. clean links in docs.

Jonas Weber: thanks all. I’ll do a quick pass to ensure methodology summary doesn’t omit anything critical (warmup/caching + derived metric definition).

Elliot Price: cool, closing loop here once PR is up.
